---
title: "EOH 635: Environmental Epidemiology Methods"
subtitle: "Asynchronous R Tutorials"
---

Welcome! These tutorials walk through the R and analysis skills used in this course. Each lesson is interactive — the code runs live, right in your browser, via [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/). You don't need R or RStudio installed to work through them.

**How to use these tutorials:**

- Read through each section, and run the code chunks as you go (click **Run Code**).
- Sections marked **🧠 Your Turn** ask you to write some code yourself before revealing the solution. Give it a real attempt first — the point is to practice, not just to read the answer.
- If you get stuck, click the collapsed "Solution" box to reveal the answer, then go back and make sure you understand *why* it works.

## Lessons

Lesson numbers match the course week. Week 1 is orientation and technical setup, so it has no tutorial.

- [Lesson 2: Intro to R and Handling Data](lesson2.qmd)
- [Lesson 3: Reading a Published Conceptual Framework](lesson3.qmd)
  — a reading/reflection activity applying exposure, outcome, mediator, confounder, and effect
  modifier vocabulary to a published greenspace-and-health framework
- [Lesson 4: Exploratory Data Analysis & Data Cleaning](lesson4.qmd)
- [Lesson 5: Exposure Assessment & Misclassification](lesson5.qmd)
  — coding decisions for a continuous exposure (NDVI), and how differential vs. non-differential
  misclassification bias an effect estimate, using a simulated dataset where the true exposure is
  known
- [Lesson 6: Regression, Linearity & Dose-Response](lesson6.qmd)
  — choosing and fitting a crude regression model (logistic vs. log-binomial) for tree canopy and
  high blood pressure, interpreting the estimate, and checking the linearity assumption with
  categorical indicator terms
- [Lesson 7: Confounding & Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs)](lesson7.qmd)
  — drawing a DAG in R to find a minimally sufficient adjustment set, then checking confounding
  in the data with the change-in-estimate approach (including modified Poisson regression when a
  log-binomial model won't converge)
- [Lesson 8: Effect Modification & Heterogeneity of Effects](lesson8.qmd)
  — asking whether the tree canopy–high blood pressure association differs by gender: stratified
  models, Cochran's Q, interaction models, and Wald and likelihood ratio tests for interaction
